problem: A data set has mean $\overset{―}{x}=6$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=10.8.$ Find the $z$-score of an observation $x=10.5,$ giving your answer to $2$ decimal places.

feedback.worked_solution:
The $z$-score of an observation $x$ is defined by

$$
z=\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{\sigma }.
$$

The $z$-score represents how many standard deviations an observation is above or below the mean of the data set.

Here, we're told that the mean is $\overset{―}{x}=4,$ and we can calculate the standard deviation as

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{0.25}=0.5.
$$

So, the $z$-score of the observation $x=3.4$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{\sigma } \\  & =\frac{3.4-4}{0.5} \\  & =-1.2.\end{aligned}
$$
